proposals: The National Horticulture Board should publish technical specifications under which a retrofitted warehouse, godown, farm outbuilding or animal shed qualifies for protected-cultivation subsidy, so conversions are not excluded simply because the scheme's paperwork assumes a new-build polyhouse.

The National Horticulture Mission should notify a separate, lower cost norm for retrofit protected-cultivation projects, so the 50% base subsidy is calculated on the walling, irrigation and ventilation actually installed rather than on a ₹12 lakh per 1,000 sq. m new structure that is not built.

State Horticulture Missions should publish each year the number of protected-cultivation applications received, approved and paid, and the subsidy disbursed, so take-up of the credit-linked, back-ended subsidy can be compared across states with different top-up rates.

ICAR should publish a list of vegetable hybrids it has evaluated for protected cultivation, by crop and region, since the research reviewed here names the lack of greenhouse-specific hybrids and the cost of exotic seed as constraints alongside capital cost.
